- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; add 0.5–1% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days after spike) — adjust forecast to align with 10–14 day moving average if sentiment is neutral.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecast using 3-day weighted average to reduce noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict mid-term recovery after downturns — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is weak and price is below 30-day MA.
